key_insight: VQE-AdvBench is the first unified red-teaming benchmark for VQE, showing that noise-pipeline attacks are the most harmful and can amplify energy error far more than circuit- or parameter-level backdoors.
engineering_relevance: For cloud-based VQE workflows, the study highlights where hardening matters most: transpilation, noise mitigation, and backend-integrity controls before trusting reported ground-state energies.
method: Builds a single evaluation protocol for VQE adversarial robustness
Organizes attacks by black-, gray-, and white-box access
Tests seven representative attacks on H2 and H3+ across five noise-calibrated IBM backends
evidence_signal: Using a fixed molecule-ansatz-backend-metric setup, the authors compare seven attacks and report up to 8.84× error amplification from noise-induced ZNE manipulation, versus 7.52× for QTrojan and 1.37× for QDoor.
watch_item: Results are benchmark-specific, so the severity ranking may shift with different ansätze, molecules, backends, or mitigation pipelines.
paper_title: SoK: Adversarial Robustness of the Variational Quantum Eigensolver via Red-Teaming
